description: The NDMC GeoPortal is the spatial data hub of South Africa's National Disaster Management Centre, built on ArcGIS Hub as part of the national disaster management information system required by the Disaster Management Act of 2002. The hub read on 2026-09-28 groups content into early warning, hazard monitoring, risk and vulnerability, climate change, disaster management tools and stakeholder reporting. The organisation's public item list shows feature services for a catalogue of historical hazardous events recorded by the South African Weather Service from 1647 to the end of 2024, MODIS fire detections from 2000 to 2026, drought index series from the Agricultural Research Council, health and education facilities drawn from OpenStreetMap in 2026, and 2011 ward tables on dwellings and access to services, plus dashboards for fire analysis, drought monitoring and initial damage assessment. Coverage is South Africa, by ward or municipality in places. Access to the public layers is free; terms of use are linked but were not read. Caveats: many items are survey forms or internal reporting tools, the facility layers are copies of OpenStreetMap, and attribute definitions were not checked. It supports hazard exposure and emergency studies, such as overlaying historical flood and storm events with health facilities by municipality. Related record: Sri Lanka's DesInventar disaster database.
